Name: CAL_fuel_usage_density
EOL Comment: Fuel density for the trip computer (raw × 0.075 g/L; stock 9867 = 740 g/L). The ECU never uses it for fuelling. It only converts injector flow × commanded pulse into reported fuel consumption: the dash economy figure (CAN 0x400) and the fuel-used counter that times the P0461 fuel-level sender check. The commanded pulse includes injector deadtime\, so each injection over-reports by roughly CAL_inj_flow_rate × deadtime of fuel that was never injected. That error grows in proportion to injector flow\, but the real fuel per injection stays the same. Leave this at the true fuel density unless you change injectors. After a swap to higher-flow injectors (or any big flow or deadtime change)\, the dash will read high consumption\, worst at idle and light load\, and P0461 may set falsely because the counter fills before the fuel level has had time to move. To restore stock-like readings\, raise this value by about (new_flow × (fuel_time + new_deadtime)) ÷ (old_flow × (old_fuel_time + old_deadtime)) at a typical cruise point. For stock → ID1050-XDS that is about 1.6–1.75×\, or roughly 16300. Then fine-tune against a measured fill-up. A single value can't be exact at every load\, because the deadtime share of the pulse falls as load rises.

Name: ign_knock_retard_octane_short_term
EOL Comment:
How it works:
- Each time a cylinder knocks\, octane_scaler_short_term[cyl] rises by ign_knock_retard × CAL_..._shortterm_multiplier.
- While there is no knock\, it decays by CAL_..._shortterm_decrement (B13200091.c:30340–30362).
- This array turns that factor into degrees.
- The long-term part (LEA_octane_scaler) scales how far the timing is pulled back toward the knock-safe map.
